reason: The jaws need a mounting point on the grabber beam, so I’ll try fitting them there.
expectation: The jaws will attach to the end of the beam.

alternatives.reason: I could check what fits the beam first.

effect: The jaws are now hinged on the beam; they still need a way to move together.
reason: The slider and guide look like the next part of the jaw mechanism.
expectation: The guided slider will attach to the beam, ready to operate the jaws through links.

effect: The slider is mounted in its guide, ready to be connected to the jaws.
reason: The separate links should connect the guided slider to the two jaws.
expectation: The links will connect the slider to both jaws so they can move together.

effect: The slider now closes both jaws through pivoting links; the mechanism still needs a return and an actuator.
reaction: The short arms spreading to close the long tips is an interesting detail.
reason: The output syringe needs a cradle to hold it in place before it can drive the mechanism.
expectation: The syringe will be secured in its cradle, ready to attach to the grabber.

effect: The output syringe is secured in its cradle and can now be fitted to the grabber.
reason: The cradled syringe should provide the actuator for the linked jaws.
expectation: The syringe assembly will attach to the grabber and connect to its slider.

effect: The output syringe is attached to the linked grabber; the jaws still need a return mechanism.
reason: The light return band should pull the mechanism back and reopen the jaws.
expectation: The band will be fitted so the jaws spring open again.

effect: The return band is fitted; the grabber is ready to test with the block.
reaction: The return mechanism went on as expected.
reason: The wooden block is the available test object for checking the jaws.
expectation: The jaws will grip the block and spring open again when released.

effect: The test confirmed that pushing the crosshead closes the jaws and releasing it lets the band reopen them. The chapter goal is complete, though remote control remains for later.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the assembled linkage grip and release the block.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the jaw links was most worthwhile: their separate pivots and short arms explained how slider movement closes the long jaw tips.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the syringe into its cradle was straightforward and revealed little on its own.

surprise.text: The short arms spread as the long jaw tips close; that clarified how the linkage reverses the movement.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The syringe's eventual remote-control role was suggested, though it was not demonstrated in this chapter.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the syringe controls the jaws from the other end, especially after testing the linkage by hand.
